Subject: RE: Randy's thyroid project. June schedule, in case you missed it. 
I . Ashley asked for update from the horse's mouth, so family and insider friends 
all get the response. 
2. All my thyroid removed this year, in two operations, one side at a time. If first 
side was benign, then don't remove second half. You can probably get by without 
medication on one side. Mine had ugly cancerous growth on first half, but not bad 
kind of cancer. 
3. Thyroid surgery does not necessarily remove all the thyroid tissue... there are 
always some fragments left. 
4. It is good to get rid of all of it, since fragments may contain cancerous tissues. 
5. Turns out, thyroid is the only tissue in the body that has an affinity for iodine. 
6. The endocrinologist plans the dose, and then you go to the hospital nuclear 
medicine department and take a radioactive iodine pill that comes in a lead box. 
7. You are in isolation for three days... can't be in the same room with anyone 
else. No sex. 
8. The radioactivity in the Iodine kills all the thyroid tissue in your body and there 
is never any more problem. 
9. Several friends have been through this, some many years ago. 
10. There are additional details in preparation, like salt free diet for week or so, 
but basically, that's the story. 
11. I have schedule this for June, so it does not interfere with other activities. 
:-) 
Randy
